comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Bank of America report on Fixed Income revenues in 2024, with both noting lower performance in rates-related areas, though BAC's disclosure is dominated by a specific index cessation charge. Citigroup reports lower rates and currencies revenues (-6%), reflecting lower volatility. Bank of America reports lower trading revenue from macro products in Fixed Income, Currencies and Commodities (FICC), but this was partially offset by a significant $1.6 billion charge from the BSBY index cessation. Both companies experienced headwinds in rates/currencies/macro products, but BAC's result was materially impacted by a one-time regulatory/structural event not cited in Citigroup's explanation.

comparisons.peer_summary: Fixed income net revenues were $8,418 million in 2024, a 10% increase from the prior year, driven by performance in Credit and Global macro products.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Morgan Stanley report revenue increases in their fixed income businesses for 2024, though the magnitude and specific drivers differ. Citigroup reports a 1% overall increase in Fixed Income Markets, driven by a 20% rise in spread products and other fixed income linked to client activity in asset-backed financing and securitization. In contrast, Morgan Stanley reports a 10% increase in Fixed Income net revenues, primarily driven by performance in Credit and Global macro products. While Citigroup highlights growth in securitization activity, Morgan Stanley points to lower losses on inventory and higher gains on rates products.
